entries.title: Proverbs 4:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A father - Of me, who have paternal authority over you and affection for you.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Tender - Young and tender in years, and tenderly educated. Only beloved - Beloved above all the rest.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Said - The following verses, at least as far as the tenth verse, are the words of David.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: With all - Even with the price of all.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Exalt - Let her have thine highest esteem and affection.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Grace - A beautiful ornament, such as they used to put upon their heads.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For - Wickedness is as pleasant to them as their bread.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: But - Just men daily grow in knowledge, and grace, and consolation, 'till all be perfected and swallowed up in glory.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Darkness - Full of ignorance and error, of uncertainty and confusion, of danger and misery.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Heart - Thy thoughts, will, and affections. For - From thence proceed all the actions, as of the natural, so of the spiritual life, which lead to eternal life.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Right on - Direct all thine actions to a right end, and keep thy mind fixed upon that way which leads to it, and neither look or turn aside to the right - hand or the left.

entries.title: Proverbs 4:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Ponder - Consider thine actions before thou dost them, and see that they agree with the rule. And - Let thine actions be uniformly and constantly good in spite of all temptations.
